contributions: Positional re-encoding: decouple KV states from RoPE rotations at storage time (store W_k x_i, W_v x_i), re-apply global rotations at concatenation, fixing the position mismatch of independently encoded segments at negligible cost.

Link tokens: K trainable tokens (e.g., K=1 or 5) appended per document with a customized attention map so each link token attends to all preceding documents' tokens plus its own document, implicitly reconnecting independently encoded segments; the LLM is fine-tuned jointly with these tokens.

Compressed KV cache linking: a modified AnLLMs that compresses fixed-length chunks into multiple anchor tokens (chunk size s=100) with chunk-local + preceding-anchor attention, reducing per-document cache storage while preserving the reuse interface.
Demonstrates that naive reuse (PromptCache) suffers up to ~35% relative accuracy drop, and that link tokens recover most of the gap to fine-tuned full-concatenation upper bound.
key_results: Backbones: Llama-3.2-1B/3B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, fine-tuned 6,000 steps, batch 64, 8xH100.

On QA (NQ, 2WikiMQA, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, MuSiQue) and summarization (MultiNews, Samsum), KVLink5 consistently beats PromptCache, CacheBlend, and BlockAttention; e.g., on Llama-3.2-1B MuSiQue: KVLink5 19.2% vs BlockAttention 14.3% vs PromptCache 1.4%; approaches the fine-tuned full-concatenation upper bound (19.9%).
TTFT: reusing precomputed KV cache reduces time-to-first-token by 85%-96% vs standard decoding; at 5,000-token context, ~96% TTFT reduction (10 reused docs of varying length).
General capability (GSM8K, MMLU, IFEval, ARC, PiQA, SciQ, Winogrande, HellaSwag): KVLink stays within ~3 points of the fine-tuned model, preserving general reasoning/instruction-following.

With cache compression (Table 3, Llama-3.2-1B): modified AnLLMs compression beats LLMLingua; KVLink5 over BlockAttention adds ~1-3 points under 50%/75% compression (e.g., HotpotQA 52.4/55.4 vs 51.1/54.3 at 75%/50%).
Link-token count monotonically helps: KVLink0 < KVLink1 < KVLink5 on most QA tasks.
limitations: Requires fine-tuning the LLM (6,000 steps) with the link-token attention mechanism — not training-free, unlike PromptCache/CacheBlend.
Link tokens and the compressed-cache variant require a customized attention mask and a training stage; integration into off-the-shelf serving stacks is non-trivial.
Storage overhead of per-document KV caches is large (e.g., ~131MB for a 1,000-token Llama3-8B cache vs ~5KB text); the compressed variant mitigates but adds a separate pretraining stage.
Evaluation contexts are moderate (1,000-5,000 tokens, 10 docs); behavior at very long contexts or very large document banks is not reported.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2026 representative of the prefix-sharing / cache-reuse route that targets the RAG/multi-query setting where the same documents recur across queries. Directly contrasts PromptCache (naive reuse, large accuracy drop), CacheBlend (partial recomputation), and BlockAttention (fine-tuning for separate encoding), and is composable with compression — supporting the contract's prefix-sharing route and the cross-route compression interaction.
analysis.summary: KVLink enables reuse of independently pre-computed per-document KV caches across different queries (e.g., RAG) by (1) storing KV states without RoPE positional embeddings and re-applying global rotary positions at inference (positional re-encoding), and (2) appending a small number of trainable 'link tokens' per document whose customized attention mask lets later documents attend back to earlier ones, restoring cross-document dependencies lost by context-free encoding. It is combined with chunked anchor-token compression (a modified AnLLMs) to cut cache storage/loading overhead.

source.title: KVLink: Accelerating Large Language Models via Efficient KV Cache Reuse

contributions: Theorem 1: bounds the attention output approximation error by ||QK^T - Q K~^T|| (amplified by V W^O) plus ||V W^O - V~ W^O||, motivating compression of the interaction KQ^T rather than K alone.
Theorem 2: closed-form optimal rank-R factorization of KQ^T via its truncated SVD (Eckart-Young), with A = K^+ U_hat, B = K^T U_hat; stores only K A* in R x T.
Efficient O(T d^2) computation by SVD-ing K and Q separately then combining on a d x d matrix, avoiding a direct T x T SVD.
Extends the same query-aware projection idea to the value-output product (Appendix B).
Theorem 4 (verified in 6.2): KQ-SVD is invariant to K/Q scaling imbalance (beta), whereas Eigen degrades toward K-SVD as imbalance grows — a robustness advantage.
key_results: Models: Llama2-7B/13B (no GQA), Llama3-8B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 (GQA); C4 dataset, 128 training sequences of 2048 tokens (T_huge=262,144), rank R chosen per layer to keep >=1-epsilon spectral energy (epsilon=0.1).
K-SVD gives the most accurate K approximation (as expected) but poor Q approximation, leading to higher attention-output error — especially in GQA models where shared K amplifies the error.
KQ-SVD matches Eigen on K/Q/V accuracy but is consistently more accurate on the attention score matrix KQ^T and on the MHA output, outperforming K-SVD and Eigen on all four models.

Unbalance experiment (Figure 2, Llama2-7B): KQ-SVD and K-SVD are scale-invariant (constant error across beta); Eigen converges to K-SVD's error as beta grows (e.g., beta=10), confirming Theorem 4 and exposing Eigen's fragility under K/Q imbalance.
Evaluation is on relative Frobenius error of K, Q, V, KQ^T, and MHA output, averaged across 32 validation sequences of 2048 tokens.
limitations: Evaluation is matrix-approximation error (Frobenius), not end-to-end task accuracy or wall-clock/throughput on long-context benchmarks; the downstream quality and speedup implications are not directly reported.
Requires a calibration set of query vectors (128 sequences) to compute projections — training-free but not zero-overhead, and projections are static once learned.
Rank R is chosen per layer from spectral energy; the compression ratio is implicit and not reported as a single headline memory-reduction figure comparable to VQKV's 82%.
GQA helps KQ-SVD relatively (it models the interaction), but the absolute error in GQA models remains higher than in non-GQA models; behavior at very large scale is not characterized.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2025-2026 representative of the low-rank compression sub-route, directly addressing the contract's compression/low-rank family. It contrasts with K-SVD (compress K alone, ignores Q) and Eigen (joint Q/K/V embedding), providing a competing-result comparison on the importance of modeling the query-key interaction. Relevant to the lossless-vs-lossy and training-free-vs-training-aware trade-offs (training-free, calibration-based).
analysis.summary: KQ-SVD is a training-free, provably optimal low-rank KV cache compression method that decomposes the query-key interaction matrix KQ^T (rather than K alone). Motivated by Theorem 1 — which bounds attention output error by the error in QK^T plus the error in V — KQ-SVD solves min_{A,B} ||K A B^T Q^T - K Q^T||_F s.t. rank<=R, and Theorem 2 gives the closed-form optimal solution A = K^+ U_hat, B = K^T U_hat where U_hat holds the top-R left singular vectors of KQ^T. Only the low-rank K A* is stored. The same strategy applies to the value-output product. Computation is O(T d^2) via SVDs of K and Q.

source.title: KQ-SVD: Compressing the KV Cache with Provable Guarantees on Attention Fidelity

contributions: Preference-prioritized adaptive allocation: a per-layer preference score P = H^(1/tau1) * V^(1/tau2) from attention entropy H and variance V over a recent observation window, normalized to distribute a global budget B_total across layers (Eq. 6-7).

Preference-guided cascading cache management: a stage-wise algorithm that maintains the budget during prefilling, reducing peak memory to the target; Theorem 1 proves it is equivalent to the optimal one-shot allocation, and Proposition 1 proves per-layer budgets decrease monotonically across stages.

Attention-shift tolerant eviction indicator: I[n] = Mean(A) + gamma*Var(A) for non-recent tokens (with a large Omega protecting the most recent W tokens), combining sustained importance and attention variability to avoid prematurely evicting fluctuating-but-important tokens.
Empirically demonstrates the allocation strategy is a generalizable framework that improves existing eviction indicators (H2O, SnapKV) when swapped in.
key_results: Evaluated on 5 LLMs (7B-70B, MHA and GQA: Llama2-Chat, Gemma-Instruct, Llama3-Instruct, Mistral-v0.3, Qwen2.5-Instruct) on LongBench (16 datasets) and NeedleBench, budgets 64L-2048L, on A100 80GB.

On LongBench at B_total=128L (Llama2-7B-Chat), CAKE averages 29.29 vs SnapKV 28.09 and PyramidKV 28.20; at 1024L, CAKE 32.98 vs SnapKV 32.50 and PyramidKV 32.55. CAKE matches full-cache performance once B_total > 512L.
On NeedleBench 32K, CAKE preserves 32K-context capability using only 3.2% of the cache and surpasses full cache on Single-Needle Retrieval; leads on Multi-Needle Retrieval.
Memory/throughput (Mistral-7B, B_total=1024L): ~48.63% peak-memory reduction vs full cache at 128K context; >10x decoding-latency speedup over full cache at 128K.

Ablation (Table 2): allocation strategies Avg — Uniform 28.36, Pyramid 28.69, Random 28.3+/-0.2, P2A 29.29. Eviction indicators (Table 3): Mean 28.82, Var 28.68, Mean*Var 28.6, Mean+Var 29.29 — additive combination best.
limitations: Training-free but requires computing attention entropy and variance over a recent window S_w at prefilling, adding a profiling pass; the cascading algorithm mitigates but does not eliminate this overhead.
Preference score depends on temperature parameters tau1, tau2 that must be tuned per model and memory constraint.
Gains over SnapKV/PyramidKV are modest in absolute terms (e.g., +0.5-1.2 LongBench points at 128L); the advantage is largest under tight budgets and narrows as budget grows toward full-cache parity.
Heuristic allocation is static per-input (computed once from prefilling attention); unlike LKV it does not learn cross-task optimal budgets.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2026 representative of the heuristic-eviction route that advances the layer-wise budget-allocation line (PyramidKV, AdaKV) with a data-driven, content-adaptive allocation plus a shift-tolerant indicator. Directly contrasts LKV (learned allocation) and SnapKV/PyramidKV (heuristic allocation), supporting the contract's eviction route and the training-free vs. training-aware trade-off. Demonstrates compatibility with existing eviction indicators (H2O, SnapKV), positioning allocation as an orthogonal axis.
analysis.summary: CAKE (Preference-prioritized Adaptive Allocation + Attention-shift tolerant Eviction) is a training-free KV cache eviction method that (1) allocates a global cache budget across layers according to a per-layer preference score combining attention spatial dispersion (entropy) and temporal shift (variance), and (2) evicts tokens using an indicator that combines mean attention (sustained importance) plus variance (attention variability) to tolerate attention shifts. A cascading cache management algorithm reduces peak prefilling memory from O(S*L) to the target budget while provably matching the result of the optimal one-shot allocation (Theorem 1).

source.title: CAKE: Cascading and Adaptive KV Cache Eviction with Layer Preferences

contributions: First end-to-end differentiable framework for KV cache eviction that jointly learns head-wise budgets and token selection, bypassing heuristic proxies entirely.
LKV-H: global 1D budget competition that flattens all L*H heads into a single Soft-TopK selection, enabling cross-layer budget transfer that rigid layer-wise heuristics cannot approximate.
LKV-T: matrix-free intrinsic token selection predicting utility from KV states alone, avoiding the chicken-and-egg problem of needing attention matrices to evaluate token importance.
Closed-form Soft-TopK operator with exact budget satisfaction, order preservation, and translation invariance, enabling stable end-to-end gradient flow.
key_results: On LongBench with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at strict 15% KV budget, LKV achieves near-lossless performance, outperforming SnapKV, PyramidKV, DuoAttention, and AdaKV.
Also evaluated on Qwen3-8B (GQA), showing compatibility with grouped-query attention; adds only ~0.1% trainable parameters.
Training is cost-effective: <2 hours on 8xA100 GPUs via self-distillation on a ~23k sample Loom dataset.
Analysis identifies learned budgeting (LKV-H) as the dominant driver of fidelity over selection policies, demonstrating data-driven allocation is essential to overcome hand-crafted heuristics.
limitations: Requires a training/distillation phase (not training-free), though lightweight (~0.1% params, <2 GPU-hours).
Learned budgets are static once trained (zero-overhead at inference but not dynamically adapted to per-input content); the global budget ratio R is fixed.
Evaluation limited to 8B-class models; scaling behavior to much larger models or extreme compression ratios below 15% is not reported in the main experiments.
analysis.relevance_to_run: Representative of the 2026 frontier in learned KV cache eviction, directly addressing the contract's eviction/token-selection route and the training-free vs. training-aware trade-off. It explicitly contrasts itself against heuristic baselines (SnapKV, PyramidKV, DuoAttention, AdaKV), providing cross-route comparison evidence.
analysis.summary: LKV formulates KV cache eviction as an end-to-end differentiable optimization problem, replacing heuristic budget allocation and token selection with learned, task-optimized policies. It has two components: LKV-H learns global head-wise budget allocation via a flattened 1D Soft-TopK competition across all layers and heads (enabling cross-layer budget transfer), and LKV-T performs matrix-free intrinsic token selection that predicts token utility from key/value states alone without materializing attention matrices. Training uses self-distillation against a frozen full-cache teacher with KL divergence on outputs plus hidden-state alignment, adding only ~0.1% trainable parameters.

source.title: LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction

contributions: Observation (Figure 2): across 200 qasper questions, max sequence length reaches 25K but unique Exact-TopK (k=256) indices only reach ~1200 — motivating two-stage eviction-then-selection to close the gap to oracle top-k attention.

Two-stage framework: coarse permanent eviction (SnapKV, per-group for GQA, pooling kernel 63) then fine dynamic selection (HSA) over the filtered set, where the reduced set makes top-k prediction far easier.

Hybrid Sparse Attention (HSA): two-dimensional reduction — page-wise element-wise max/min along the sequence (Quest-style) plus head-dimension magnitude sparsity (SparQ-style) — approximating top-k attention scores with both K_max and K_min and a sign-based fetch.
Adaptive compression decomposition: split factor r = min(0.2+0.06*log2(c), 0.8) balances the two stages; HSA evenly splits its ratio across sequence and head dims.
RocketKV-MT: multi-turn variant retaining full KV history across turns (no storage saving) but filtering per-turn for decode speed, eliminating permanent-eviction loss in multi-turn settings.
System integration: compatible with FlashAttention (prefill untouched), tensor parallelism, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving (reduces KV transfer traffic).
key_results: Evaluated on Llama3.1-8B-Ins, Mistral-7B-Ins-v0.2, LongChat-7B-v1.5 (GQA + MHA) on LongBench, NIAH, RULER, SCBench; token budgets 256-4096 (single-turn), 1024-16384 (SCBench multi-turn).
LongBench (Llama3.1-8B-Ins): RocketKV near-lossless at budget >=512, only 1.1% avg drop at 256; consistently beats SnapKV, Quest, SparQ, DuoAttention, with the gap widening at low budgets.
NIAH (Llama3.1-8B-Ins): 100% accuracy at 256-token budget = >400x compression at 109K max sequence length; SnapKV drops >20% on Mistral/LongChat even at 1024.
RULER: accuracy loss negligible at short lengths, growing beyond models' effective context; RocketKV's advantage over baselines widens at longer sequences.
SCBench (multi-turn): RocketKV-MT matches Exact-TopK across all budgets, fixing the multi-turn accuracy gap that plain RocketKV suffers vs SparQ at high budgets.
Efficiency (Llama3.1-8B-Ins FP16, batch 1): up to 3.7x end-to-end speedup on A100 and 3.3x on H100, up to 32.6% peak memory saving; A100 speedup > H100 because A100 is more memory-bound.
Storage/traffic analysis (Table 1): at compression ratio c, RocketKV storage = 1/c^r + 2/c^((1+r)/2), traffic = 1/c; RocketKV-MT storage = 1 + 2/c^((1+r)/2) (no first-stage storage saving).
limitations: Two-stage pipeline adds implementation complexity (SnapKV + HSA kernels, auxiliary K_max/K_min storage); the Python/gpt-fast prototype is not yet CUDA-optimized, so wall-clock gains could be larger with FlashInfer-style kernels.
RocketKV (single-turn) still shows an accuracy gap to Exact-TopK on SCBench multi-turn at high budgets; only RocketKV-MT closes it, at the cost of no storage saving.
Stage-1 SnapKV pooling kernel (63) and the split factor formula are empirically tuned; transfer across models/tasks is not fully validated.
Evaluated at 7B-8B scale; behavior at much larger models and the interaction with grouped-query vs multi-head attention is partially covered but not exhaustive.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2026 representative that fuses the eviction route (Stage 1, SnapKV) with the dynamic sparse-selection route (Stage 2, Quest/SparQ-style), directly addressing the contract's eviction, sparsity, and cross-route composition themes. It provides the key cross-route insight that single-stage/single-dimension methods hit an accuracy wall at high compression, while two-stage two-dimensional decomposition preserves accuracy to much higher ratios — a concrete competing-result comparison against SnapKV, Quest, SparQ, DuoAttention.
analysis.summary: RocketKV is a two-stage decode-phase KV cache compression framework: Stage 1 performs coarse-grained permanent eviction (SnapKV with per-group selection and a larger pooling kernel of 63) to keep most important tokens; Stage 2 performs fine-grained dynamic top-k selection via Hybrid Sparse Attention (HSA), which reduces along both sequence and head dimensions using element-wise page max/min key statistics. An adaptive split factor r = min(0.2+0.06*log2(c), 0.8) allocates the overall compression ratio c across the two stages. A multi-turn variant RocketKV-MT retains full KV history across turns (no storage saving) but filters per turn for decode speed, avoiding permanent-eviction accuracy loss in multi-turn dialogue.

source.title: RocketKV: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Two-Stage KV Cache Compression

contributions: Arithmetic-intensity / roofline analysis of prefill vs. decoding across (small/large batch) x (short/long context) regimes, classifying which regimes are weight-quantization-bound vs. KV-cache-quantization-bound.

Hierarchical INT4 KV cache: INT8 = 2^4 * C_U^INT4 + C_L^INT4, letting the draft model use the upper 4 bits and the target model reconstruct INT8 from both halves, removing the redundant draft KV copy.

Double full-precision buffer (2G) that keeps recent tokens in FP16 for high acceptance rate, defers quantization to every G steps, and cleanly supports speculative-decoding rollback by operating only on the second buffer.
Self-speculative decoding with shared architecture (draft = INT4 upper bits, target = INT8 reconstruction), improving acceptance rate over big-little speculative decoding.
key_results: INT8 KV cache perplexity on Llama-2-7B (WikiText2 6.4696 vs FP16 6.4595; C4 7.2620 vs 7.2617) — near-lossless, validating INT8 as the target precision.

On Llama-2-7B-32K-Instruct and LWM-Text-Chat-128k, QuantSpec achieves up to 2.49x speedup over autoregressive (AR) target generation, vs sparsity-based self-speculative baselines (StreamingLLM, SnapKV).
At 128k context (LWM-Text-Chat, Multi-LexSum), StreamingLLM and SnapKV hit OOM while QuantSpec runs at 61.22 GB peak memory with 94.31% acceptance and 2.49x speedup.
At 32k (Llama-2-7B, Multi-LexSum): QuantSpec 2.08x speedup, 25.84 GB vs StreamingLLM 1.84x/32.61GB and SnapKV 1.63x/33.96GB; acceptance 91.16%.
Quantization strategy: key cache quantized along channel axis, value cache along token axis (per-group, group size G = head dim), minimizing quantization error and maximizing acceptance.
limitations: Self-speculative: the draft and target share architecture, so speedup is bounded by the acceptance rate and the INT4-vs-INT8 compute ratio; gains are largest in long-context memory-bound regimes.
The double full-precision buffer adds 2G tokens of FP16 KV per layer, partially offsetting the compression benefit.
Reported on Llama-2-7B-class models; scaling to much larger models and the interaction with GQA/MoE is not fully characterized.
Acceptance rate can dip below baselines in some short-context regimes (e.g., 8k PG19 89.88% vs SnapKV 94.39%), though end-to-end speedup still wins.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2025 representative of the speculative-decoding × KV-cache interaction route, directly addressing the contract's speculative/parallel decoding interaction with cache. It is grounded in an arithmetic-intensity / roofline analysis that explains when weight quantization vs. KV-cache quantization dominates, and it composes quantization with self-speculative decoding — a cross-route combination distinct from pure eviction or pure compression.
analysis.summary: QuantSpec is a self-speculative decoding framework that accelerates both short- and long-context generation by quantizing model weights and the KV cache to INT4. Its core innovation is a hierarchical INT4 KV cache: an INT8 value is decomposed into upper and lower 4-bit halves, so the draft model loads only the upper INT4 (fast, low-precision) while the target model reconstructs INT8 from both halves (high precision) — eliminating the redundant separate draft KV cache. A double full-precision buffer of size 2G (G = quantization group size) keeps the most recent tokens in full precision to maintain a high draft acceptance rate and to handle speculative-decoding rollbacks without repeated quantize/dequantize overhead.

source.title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache

contributions: Three-level hybrid design: (L1) architectural hybrid of RNN matrix memory + softmax attention; (L2) intra-layer hybrid concatenating long-term (m-slot gated RNN) and short-term (w-window) memory under a unified softmax; (L3) inter-layer hybrid by varying w per layer (w=0 pure linear, w=N full attention).
Unified softmax fusion over concatenated long+short memory, which gradient analysis shows couples gradient flow between the two memories better than output-level weighted fusion.
Chunkwise parallel form enabling efficient training (analogous to GSA's associative scan), with linear memory update + shifted sliding-window logits fused in one softmax.
Pretrained-LLM hybridization: replacing selected full-attention layers of Llama-3-8B / Qwen2.5-7B / Qwen3-30B-A3B with NHA modules + lightweight fine-tuning, reducing reliance on full attention.
key_results: Pretrained from scratch at 340M/15B tokens and 1.3B/100B tokens with 'one Transformer every 8 layers' stacking. At 1.3B, NHA averages 46.43 on recall-intensive tasks (FDA/SWDE/SQuAD/NQ/TriviaQA/Drop) vs GDN-H 44.88, GSA-H 44.99, Mamba2-H 44.18; and 52.89 commonsense avg, competitive with best hybrids.
RULER long-context (trained 2K, tested to 8K): NHA 81.4/51.8/21.6 on NIAH-MK (1K/2K/4K) vs GDN-H 59.6/29.4/15.0; strongest extrapolation among hybrids, though Transformer still leads in-length NIAH.

Pretrained-LLM hybridization: NHA-Llama-3-8B (4 full-attn layers) achieves best recall avg (57.64) among same-scale hybrids with the fewest full-attention layers, closely matching original Llama-3-8B (60.08).
Scaling to Qwen3-30B-A3B: NHA hybrid (47.25 avg) stays competitive with the original (44.60) on a broad benchmark suite including GPQA/IFVL/HEval/MaQA/MMLU.

Operator efficiency (H100): NHA scales near-linearly and matches GSA speed across lengths; FlashAttention is faster on short sequences but quadratic on long. NHA-Llama3-8B inference latency/memory grow much slower than Llama3-8B at 1K-token generation.

Ablation (Table 5): removing long-term memory drops recall 38.60->29.58; removing short-term 36.97; removing token shift 35.76; unified softmax (38.60) beats weighted-sum fusion variants (34.06 fixed, 33.59 learnable).
limitations: Requires from-scratch pretraining for the full benefit; the pretrained-LLM hybridization path uses a limited (~10B-token) fine-tuning budget and shows a gap on recall-intensive tasks and MMLU, partly attributed to data distribution shift and 2K training context.
Long-term memory is fixed-size (m slots), so exact retrieval of arbitrarily old tokens is fundamentally bounded — pure Transformers still lead on in-length needle-in-a-haystack.
Reported hybrid ratios use a small number of full-attention layers (e.g., 4); the optimal layer placement and ratio for larger models is not fully characterized.
Comparison is at 340M/1.3B from scratch and 7B-30B hybridized; the compute cost of from-scratch NHA pretraining at frontier scale is not reported.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2026 representative of the architectural-alternatives route (linear/SSM + attention hybrids), directly addressing the contract's architectural-alternatives family. It unifies the 'one Transformer every N layers' hybrid pattern into a single intra-layer mechanism and contrasts with NSA (natively trainable sparse) and Mamba-2/GSA/GLA/GDN pure-linear baselines, supporting cross-route comparison between sparse-attention and linear-memory hybrids.
analysis.summary: Native Hybrid Attention (NHA) is a unified attention architecture that fuses, within a single layer, a fixed-size gated linear-RNN long-term memory (m slots) with a sliding-window short-term memory (w tokens), applying softmax over their concatenated keys. By varying the window size w per layer, the same module can act as pure linear RNN (w=0), intra-layer hybrid (0<w<N), or full attention (w=N), enabling inter-layer hybridization without architectural changes. NHA also supports a chunkwise parallel form for efficient training and can retrofit pretrained Transformers into NHA hybrids with lightweight fine-tuning.

source.title: Native Hybrid Attention for Efficient Sequence Modeling

contributions: A standardized KV caching layer between inference engines and heterogeneous storage, compatible with vLLM and SGLang, exposing store/retrieve/lookup interfaces and a shared token pool for cross-instance cache awareness.
Chunk-level KV transfer (vs vLLM's page-by-page) using high-performance CUDA kernels, achieving 400 Gbps CPU loading bandwidth vs vLLM native 88 Gbps (Table 5).
Asynchronous, layer-wise KV loading overlapped with prefill/decode compute (request asynchronization), reducing end-to-end delay by 1.46x.

Adaptive KV-loading-vs-prefill decision: at low network bandwidth (32 Gbps) loading beats prefill only beyond 256K tokens; at 64/128 Gbps it wins across all lengths — a deployment-condition guideline.
Efficient PD disaggregation via chunked GPU-buffer transfer between prefetcher and decoder, improving tail TTFT over vLLM's native NIXL page-by-page transfer.
key_results: Models: Llama-3.1-8B/70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, Qwen2.5-72B, Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B (FP8), Sao10K-L3-8B; hardware 8xH100 (GMI Cloud).

Single-node CPU offloading (multi-round Q&A, 10K-token queries, 500GB CPU DRAM): 1.9-8.1x smaller TTFT and 2.3-14x higher throughput than the strongest baseline across 5 models; 7-92% smaller ITL at QPS=1. Commercial options cannot host Qwen3-Coder-480B.
Real-trace (companies F and G): 3.7-6.8x smaller TTFT and 19-58% smaller ITL vs basic vLLM at high QPS.
Centralized remote storage (15 Gbps, TriviaQA): 1.3-3x throughput improvement; remote loading can exceed prefill delay for short contexts / small models, motivating adaptive loading.
PD disaggregation (8K input / 200 output): 1.53-1.84x lower mean TTFT and 1.12-1.66x lower mean ITL than vLLM native PD disaggregation; significantly better tail (p95) TTFT.
SGLang integration (Qwen3-32B, TP=2): higher throughput / lower TTFT than SGLang without offloading; comparable to SGLang native offloading but with hierarchical distributed backend support.
limitations: Gains depend on cache hit ratio, which depends on workload prefix overlap; for low-overlap workloads the CPU/remote storage benefit shrinks.
Remote-backend loading is bandwidth-bound: at 32 Gbps it only beats prefill beyond 256K tokens, so adaptive gating is required and benefit is not universal.
Evaluation is system-level (TTFT/ITL/throughput) rather than accuracy-preserving compression; LMCache is orthogonal to (and composable with) accuracy-affecting methods like quantization/eviction.
Commercial baselines are black-box; internal implementation differences are hypothesized, not verified.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2025-2026 representative of the prefix-sharing / caching-systems and system/scheduling/offloading route, directly addressing the contract's prefix-sharing and system-scheduling families. It complements algorithmic KV compression (VQKV, RocketKV) by tackling the storage/movement/sharing axis, and provides deployment-condition evidence (TTFT, ITL, throughput, bandwidth) across 8B-480B models — supporting the contract's deployment-conditions requirement.
analysis.summary: LMCACHE is a unified, high-performance KV caching layer that sits between paged-memory LLM inference engines (vLLM, SGLang) and heterogeneous storage/network backends (GPU, CPU DRAM, remote disks), making prefix caching, CPU offloading, cross-instance KV sharing, and prefill/decode (PD) disaggregation practical at enterprise scale. Its architecture comprises a KV connector, token processor, storage manager, transfer channel, event manager, and a cache controller with a shared token pool. Key performance techniques include chunk-level (vs page-level) transfers, asynchronous layer-wise loading overlapped with compute, and adaptive decisions between KV loading and prefilling depending on bandwidth and context length.

source.title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference

contributions: Applies Residual Simple Vector Quantization (RSimVQ) — combining Residual VQ with SimVQ projection matrices — to KV cache, storing only codebook indices instead of full-precision vectors.
Integrates VQ compression into both prefilling (batch compression of the prompt KV) and decoding (per-token compression with a sliding local window of full-precision entries).
On-demand reconstruction from codebooks during attention, keeping codebooks resident while storing only integer codes for the bulk of the cache.
Achieves high compression ratios (~82-83%) with fidelity closer to full cache than feature-dimension-reduction and scalar-quantization baselines.
key_results: Compression ratio of 82.8% on LLaMA3.1-8B and 82.4% on LLaMA3.2-3B.
On LongBench, VQKV achieves the closest performance to full-cache models among comparable-ratio methods, outperforming ASVD, Palu, KIVI, and SnapKV.
Codebook configuration for LLaMA3.1-8B: (N_k, N_v) = (56, 16) codebooks, sizes (S_k, S_v) = (1024, 512); for LLaMA3.2-3B: (N_k, N_v) = (56, 10), sizes (1024, 65536).
RSimVQ trained on 0.1% of OpenWebText with learning rate 0.001, batch size 65536; initial tokens L_init=4, local window L_local=1024.
Memory-efficiency test shows VQKV extends maximum generation length beyond full-cache under identical hardware.
limitations: Requires offline training of RSimVQ codebooks (lightweight, on 0.1% of OpenWebText) — not purely training-free, though no LLM fine-tuning is needed.
Codebook size and count must be tuned per model and per K/V cache type, adding configuration complexity.
Reconstruction introduces lookup overhead; net wall-clock speedup depends on codebook residency and memory-bandwidth trade-offs not fully detailed in the experiment section.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A 2026 frontier representative of the vector-quantization sub-route within KV cache compression, directly relevant to the contract's compression/quantization route and the lossless-vs-lossy trade-off. Contrasts scalar quantization (KIVI), low-rank approximation (ASVD, Palu), and eviction (SnapKV) under matched compression ratios.
analysis.summary: VQKV compresses the KV cache via Residual Simple Vector Quantization (RSimVQ), mapping each KV vector to indices in multiple residual-connected codebooks with an extra projection matrix per codebook. Only codebooks and integer codes are stored, and reconstruction is on-demand from codebooks during attention. It achieves high compression ratios (~82-83%) while preserving fidelity closer to full-cache than scalar quantization (KIVI) or low-rank methods (ASVD, Palu).

source.title: VQKV: High-Fidelity and High-Ratio Cache Compression via Vector-Quantization

contributions: Hierarchical sparse attention combining three branches: compressed block-level attention (coarse), top-k selected block attention (fine), and sliding-window local attention, fused via learned gating.
Natively trainable: the sparse pattern is learned during pretraining rather than fixed at inference, so the model adapts to sparsity during training.
Hardware-aligned kernel design balancing arithmetic intensity so that decoding becomes memory-bandwidth-efficient, achieving real wall-clock speedup rather than theoretical-only FLOP reduction.
End-to-end pretraining at scale (27B total / 3B active GQA+MoE) demonstrating sparse attention can match or exceed full attention quality.
key_results: Backbone: 27B total / 3B active parameters, GQA (64 heads, 4 groups) + DeepSeekMoE (72 routed + 2 shared experts, top-6), 30 layers.
Pretrained on 270B tokens of 8k-length texts, then continued training + SFT on 32k-length texts with YaRN for long-context adaptation.
NSA consistently achieves lower pretraining loss than the Full Attention baseline trained to convergence under identical settings.

Matches or improves over Full Attention on general benchmarks (MMLU, MMLU-PRO, CMMLU, BBH, GSM8K, MATH, DROP, MBPP, HumanEval) and long-context benchmarks, while delivering substantial training and inference speedup.
Hyperparameters: compression block size 32, stride 16, selected block size 64, selected block count 16 (1 initial + 2 local fixed), sliding window 512.
limitations: Requires natively training the model from scratch with the sparse attention mechanism; not a drop-in training-free method for existing pretrained LLMs.
The sparse pattern and gating are learned during pretraining, so the benefit is tied to models trained this way rather than retrofitted to off-the-shelf models like Llama/Qwen.
Reported at a specific 27B/3B MoE scale; transfer of the exact sparse configuration to dense models of other sizes is not fully characterized in the main text.
analysis.relevance_to_run: A seminal 2025 work for the sparse-attention architectural route, co-designed with hardware to address the gap between theoretical sparsity and real speedup. It represents the 'natively trainable sparse attention' sub-route and is widely cited by 2026 follow-ups (UNIQUE, SPLA, Token Sparse Attention). Directly relevant to the contract's sparsity and architectural-alternative routes.
analysis.summary: NSA (Native Sparse Attention) is a hardware-aligned, natively trainable hierarchical sparse attention mechanism that combines coarse-grained token block compression with fine-grained token selection and sliding-window local attention. It is designed to be trained end-to-end from scratch rather than applied as a post-hoc inference trick, and includes arithmetic-intensity-balanced kernel optimizations so that sparse attention is actually faster in practice, not just in FLOP count.

source.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
